title: Cron scheduled tasks

requirements.text: Cron expressions are parsed and invalid expressions are rejected when the schedule is saved
The next run time is computed correctly, including the day-of-month/day-of-week rule and leap days
Schedules are evaluated in a configured IANA time zone and stay correct across DST changes
Each occurrence runs once even with several application instances
A run that is still executing does not overlap the next occurrence unless allowed
Occurrences missed during downtime follow a declared catch-up or skip policy
Failed runs are retried or reported according to policy

evidence.name: parseCron accepts ranges, steps, lists, names, Sunday as 0 or 7, and @macros
parseCron rejects malformed expressions with the failing field
saving a schedule rejects invalid cron, unknown zones, unknown handlers and never-matching dates
nextOccurrence follows the Vixie day-of-month OR day-of-week rule and leap days in UTC
America/New_York spring forward: a time in the skipped hour runs once at the next valid instant
America/New_York fall back: an ambiguous time runs once, at its first occurrence
schedules are evaluated in an IANA zone with Intl, including offsets and day boundaries
three concurrent instances on one store run each occurrence exactly once
three concurrent instances on PGlite run each occurrence exactly once
the unique (schedule_id, scheduled_for) claim rejects a second materialization of one occurrence
overlap skip: an occurrence due while the previous run holds a live lease is skipped and recorded
overlap queue: the next occurrence waits until the running one finishes, then runs
lease heartbeat keeps a long run owned
overlap skip and queue hold a slot on PostgreSQL
catchUp none skips occurrences missed during downtime but runs an on-time one
catchUp latest runs only the most recent missed occurrence
catchUp all runs missed occurrences oldest first, capped to the most recent maxCatchUp
catch-up policies after downtime on PostgreSQL: none, latest and all with a cap
failed runs retry with exponential backoff up to maxAttempts, then call onFailure with history
a crash during the final attempt fails the run without executing again
schema applies and the SQL store keeps schedules, history, retries and onFailure

implementations.notes: At-least-once execution: a crash after the handler's work but before the run is marked finished runs it again, so handlers must be idempotent. A repeated fall-back wall time runs once; use UTC for interval-style jobs. PGlite concurrency tests run on one connection.

evidence.name: cron-next: vectors including Vixie day rule and leap day
cron-next: vectors including Vixie day rule and leap day

implementations.notes: pg-boss schedule/unschedule with time zones and retries; scheduler execution is not exercised by the pack tests

notes: module:scheduled-tasks covers parsing, next runs in an IANA zone across DST, one run per occurrence across instances, overlap policies with leases, catch-up policies and retries. The app calls tick() from its own interval or platform cron, and handlers must be idempotent.
